Crested Darrok.description:
Crested darroks are massive reptilian beasts native to the swampy wetlands of Rodnarth. Solitary and territorial, darroks spend most of the year swimming in murky swamps and basking in the sun, avoiding contact with other members of their species. Once a year, however, darroks leave their solitude behind, forming a huge herd that travels deep into the swamp to find sheltered waters for their spawning ponds.

During migrations, darroks search for suitable partners through displays of agility and strength. These take the form of dances and races that members of both sexes use to show of their fitness, as well as elaborate vocal performances. True violence among darroks is incredibly rare, and most disputes are solved by the quick flashing of a sonic crest or a powerful screech. If rivalries escalate into physical aggression, matriarchs lead their herds in a hauntingly soft song to restore the peace.

When a herd is threatened or loses its matriarch, darroks are capable of incredible destruction. Before the poaching of darrok matriarchs was banned planet-wide, every year, many settlements were regularly flattened by a darrok stampedes.

Crystal-Pulse Construct.description:
A crystal-pulse construct is a volatile and unpredictable creature, formed when an electrical field holds magically charged crystals in suspension. Existing in a constant state of flux, the construct must vent magical and electrical energy almost constantly to stabilize its form.

While crystal-pulse constructs sometimes form spontaneously when lightning strikes a magical environment or other powerful currents encounter magically charged minerals, only deliberately calibrated constructs have the necessary equilibrium to remain animated for long. These stabler constructs are most commonly found guarding the laboratories of wizards and elementalists or wandering the Plane of Metal.

2JmDrtvhB4DzRTvk.description:

If the triggering effect had the electricity trait, this is electricity damage, and if it was triggered by a spell, this is force damage. If the reaction is triggered by an electricity spell, the damage is either electricity or force, whichever would be more detrimental to creatures in the area, as determined by the GM.

Mannoq Beast.description:
The famously inhospitable swamps of the planet Rodnarth are subject to a variety of extreme weather events, from the sulfur-filled waterways igniting in flash firestorms to invisible deposits of lethal gases.

The flora and fauna of Rodnarth have adapted to be similarly extreme. The mannoq beast (Rodnarthian for "fire eater") is one such example. Mannoq beasts are plantlike creatures that have evolved to feed on the swamps' frequent firestorms and repurpose the resulting chemicals into their sap and fruits. Their violent method of reproduction is often misconstrued as aggression: instead of encouraging animals to eat their fruit to spread seeds, mannoq beasts launch explosive fruit whenever they detect motion. Upon striking a target, the plum-like fruit bursts into caustic, sticky sap. As the victim attempts to flee, the seeds held within the sap gradually fall off and germinate.

Though they've shown some rudimentary capacity for understanding language, only the bravest (or luckiest) naturalists have made any progress forming an accord with these creatures, most often in the form of trading chemical nutrients for the chance to pick their fruit in peace.

It can use its extra action to Stride or Strike. Conversely, when a mannoq beast takes cold damage, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Mutant Bastorox.description:
The dreaded bastoroxes are bio-organic bulwarks that use an immense chitinous shield to deflect damage while loosing bolts of bioelectricity at foes. They hold positions for advancing Krethiskar subcolony components, such as the multitudes of agile emganats. These biohulks are but one of the new innovations found within the ranks of the Krethiskar subcolony, and they were active during the siege of Rodnarth, where they implacably advanced through that world's treacherous swamps.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

Nursery Drone.description: Caypins are brawny predators with the agility of wolves and the scaly skin of crocodiles. Their most striking feature is a mass of wriggling, semi-sentient appendages that cover their heads. Each of these tentacle-like protuberances contains a bloodshot eyeball and a gaping mouth full of teeth, and the caypin—which has no eyes or mouth of its own—relies on these orifices to see and feed. Nutrients absorbed by the appendages are passed to the caypin via tiny receptive sockets in the beast's jaw, and caypins can detach these appendages into writhing clusters that independently move up to 100 feet from their bodies. Ravenous Szynegator Swarm.description:
A single szynegator vibrating causes slight vertigo, but when these tiny beetle-like components harmonize, the atmospheric disruption they generate renders most forms of communication inoperable. Szynegators can usually be found in isolated or desolate areas of planets so their number can grow unimpeded. Their presence harbingers a full Swarm invasion.

Developing far out in the Vast from an insectile species known as kucharns, the Swarm is considered the greatest threat in existence for several cultures. Composed of countless subcolonies, each consisting of myriad component subspecies, the Swarm is a vast host that acts in psychic union for the purpose of consuming all matter across the cosmos. Most frightening of all is the Swarm's ability to assimilate the knowledge and DNA of those they consume. Thanks to its pre-Gap development of star travel, the Swarm had already consumed innumerable systems before history short-circuited, and the Swarm's pace only accelerated once it received access to the Signal and the hyperspace dimension known as the Drift.

Worlds touched by the Swarm are drained of their natural resources and rendered barren places known as huskworlds. What outsiders consider to be "Swarm space" is little more than a swathe of lifeless worlds that the Swarm have consumed in its reckless advance. The Swarm so thoroughly strips these worlds that surveyors struggle to find even trace amounts of inorganic resources, such as rare minerals and water. Few of these huskworlds have been thoroughly explored, as oftentimes exploration awakens inert drones, theorized to have been left behind in case the devoured system was ever colonized and repopulated. Pockets of Swarm activity exist well beyond this region of space, as the Swarm sent out countless subcolonies in the ages before the Gap, and even now, only some of them have reached their intended destinations.

The Swarm is perhaps most known in the current era for two important facts. First, its assault on the Pact Worlds and the Veskarium led to the cessation of hostilities and tenuous alliance between the two powers. Second, the Swarm is the direct ancestor of the shirren species. Having broken away sometime during the Gap, shirrens found succor with the deity Hylax, who was believed to have evolved from a pre-Swarm kucharn and who turned her back on the ravenous entity the Swarm has evolved into.

In recent years, the Swarm had been seen as little more than a distant boogeyman with no activities save for classified actions in the Suskillon system in the Vast. However, the recent discovery of the missing Szandite world of Krethiskar inadvertently awoke a dormant subcolony that had been responsible for the world's consumption. Since then, the newly dubbed Krethiskar subcolony has become a scourge of Near Space, engaged in an active invasion of Szandite Collective worlds and poised to spill over into other powers like the Veskarium and Pact Worlds. This rediscovered subcolony has begun rapid evolution of its components and remains cut off from the wider Swarm, but it still represents a clear danger to Near Space.

While most types of fey come into being as the guardians of natural phenomena, some declare themselves the stewards of mortal creations, such as buildings or starships. Shiptreeks are a name given to the variety of small fey who bond to starships and task themselves with their chosen craft's care and upkeep. They often live in family groups numbering between 10 and 20 members.

While shiptreeks are often mistaken for gremlins, these reclusive fey bear no ill will toward others. Problems most often arise because the shiptreeks' sole loyalty is to their bonded ship, and they typically spare no thought for the actual crew of that ship. They don't like to be observed, coming out of hiding when members of the crew are elsewhere to repair and maintain their bonded ship.

Though they can be helpful, shiptreeks often consider anything within their bonded starship to belong to them, and crews unaware of shiptreeks' presence often end up at each other's throats, slinging accusations of stealing belongings and pilfering rations. In addition, anyone who disrespects their bonded ship (which can take a variety of forms, depending on the shiptreeks in question) is inevitably harassed until they disembark or make amends.

However, a crew that can come to an agreement with a shiptreek crew, usually through regular offerings of food or trinkets, often has one of the best-running starships in the system.

Subranox.name: Subranox

Surging Consoles.description: Surging electricity from the damaged power core has charged the consoles in this module with magical electricity, which arcs toward any creature that gets too close to the core.
Surging Consoles.hazardDisable: @Check[crafting|dc:22] (trained) or @Check[Physical Science Lore|dc:18] (trained) to safely ground the electricity, @Check[arcana|dc:22] (trained) or Occultism (trained) to redirect the magical component of the electricity, or @Check[crafting|dc:25] to improvise equipment to safely manipulate the console; three total successes are needed to disable the hazard
Surging Consoles.hazardReset: The fluctuating power core recharges the electricity surging through the consoles after 1 minute, after which the hazard can trigger again. Repairing the power core permanently disables the hazard.
Surging Consoles.hazardRoutine: (2 actions) The surging electricity arcs from the consoles to up to two creatures within 10 feet, dealing @Damage[(2d8+5)[electricity]] damage to each (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save).
Surging Consoles.name: Surging Consoles

Swarm Nullifier.description: Quivering Swarm biomass covers the metal dish of an old abandoned signal repeater.
Swarm Nullifier.hazardDisable: @Check[computers|dc:26] or @Check[crafting|dc:26] to shut down the amplifier, @Check[medicine|dc:26] to inject the biomass with an inhibitor (automatic if the PCs use the sedative they created by earning 7 or more Research Points)
Swarm Nullifier.hazardReset: The trap resets immediately after 1 minute (or after 15 minutes if injected with the experimental inhibitor).
Swarm Nullifier.name: Swarm Nullifier

Swarm Turret.description: The szynegation hub rearranges its scavenged walls to reveal a mounted gun turret aimed at the room's occupants.
Swarm Turret.hazardDisable: @Check[computers|dc:27] (expert) or Medicine (expert) to reprogram the turret, @Check[crafting|dc:29] (expert) to sever the power source, @Check[thievery|dc:26] (expert) to disable the turret
Swarm Turret.hazardReset: (3 actions) The trap makes a laser bile Strike against up to three creatures in range or multiple Strikes against one creature in range if it has no additional targets.
Swarm Turret.name: Swarm Turret

BuO4uNoat356mTfn.description: The szandite cryshard swarm collapses into its natural form: a Huge sea of tiny szandite crystals. It drops anything it's holding. While in swarm form, the szandite cryshard swarm's Speed is 25 feet, it can move through any area large enough for a single crystal to fit through without having to Squeeze, and it gains Engulf.
BuO4uNoat356mTfn.name: Swarm Form

NEl8kAqjZcIreAWr.description:
Requirements The szandite cryshard swarm is in swarm form

Effect The szandite cryshard swarm coalesces into a Huge shape that looks like a humanoid or beast and can hold items.

In battle form, its Speed is 15 feet, it's @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, and it has the following Strike.

Melee 1 limb +19 (reach 20 feet), Damage 4d8+9 bludgeoning
NEl8kAqjZcIreAWr.name: Battle Form

lSzDT5Nsmf0SowLo.description: When a szandite cryshard swarm takes mental damage, they automatically shift into swarm form.
lSzDT5Nsmf0SowLo.name: Psychic Dispersal

44cHltfClJj9veWk.description: A szandite stalker can perfectly mimic the voice of a creature it has observed speaking and can project this voice psychically via its szandite crystals to any creatures within 100 feet. Any creature the stalker communicates with in this manner must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23] save or believe the mimicry to be true.
44cHltfClJj9veWk.name: Psychic Mimicry

NK2r2Duy4qvQmIeL.description: The szandite stalker designates a single creature they can see and hear, or one they're Tracking, as their prey. The szandite stalker gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [[/act seek]] the prey and to Survival checks to [[/act track]] the prey. The first time the szandite stalker hits their designated prey in a round, they deal an additional 1d8 precision damage. These effects last until the szandite stalker uses Hunt Prey again.
NK2r2Duy4qvQmIeL.name: Hunt Prey

OrPqjaH7zzU6DyKd.description:
After the szandite stalker attempts a Strike at a Large or smaller target (regardless of success or failure), the next Strike one of the stalker's allies makes against the same target gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.P0PjncVUqsdDFfhv]{Effect: Coordinated Hunt}
OrPqjaH7zzU6DyKd.name: Coordinated Hunt

yr9fik09YCYCmjmm.description: The szandite stalker Strides twice, each time in a straight line. Once per Stride, it can attempt a bladed limb Strike against a creature in its reach at any point during its movement; it must make each attack against a different creature, but it doesn't apply its multiple attack penalty until after making both Strikes.
yr9fik09YCYCmjmm.name: Slide and Slash

Szynegator Egg Sac.description: An ovular alien egg sac emerges from the ground or other surface; pulsing, veinlike filaments cover all surfaces in a 30-foot radius around the egg sac.
Szynegator Egg Sac.hazardDisable: @Check[nature|dc:30] (trained) to cause the egg sac to implode, or @Check[survival|dc:23] (expert) to safely destroy the filaments in an adjacent square
Szynegator Egg Sac.hazardReset: If the egg sac survives and hasn't hatched, filaments regrow in 1 day.
Szynegator Egg Sac.name: Szynegator Egg Sac

0p1NhIRJKhPkA0yM.description: When the techno graveknight is destroyed, their armor rebuilds their body over the course of 1d10 days—or more quickly if the armor is worn by a living host (see graveknight's curse). If the body is destroyed before then, the process restarts. The techno graveknight can only be permanently destroyed by obliterating their armor (such as with disintegrate), transporting it to the Forge of Creation, or throwing it into the heart of a volcano, star, black hole, or similarly destructive environment.
0p1NhIRJKhPkA0yM.name: Rejuvenation

1sPvlKhfN4HvC7sb.description: The techno graveknight unleashes a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] that deals @Damage[11d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save). The techno graveknight can use this ability once every [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.
1sPvlKhfN4HvC7sb.name: Devastating Blast

Uo1SiUQtSoOdbmem.description:
This curse affects anyone who wears a techno graveknight's armor for at least 1 hour, unless the curse is removed

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:29] save

Onset 1 hour

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2}, –10-foot status penalty to Speeds, and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 3 dies and transforms into the armor's graveknight.
Uo1SiUQtSoOdbmem.name: Graveknight's Curse

bTBAY7TXxTQIIvxs.description:
Any weapon the techno graveknight wields gains the effects of a commercial shock module.

Additionally, the techno graveknight has access to the critical specialization effects of any weapons they wield.
bTBAY7TXxTQIIvxs.name: Techno Armaments

tWwpnS8heqbG9VQe.description: 30 feet. When a creature in the aura uses a vitality spell or ability, the graveknight automatically attempts to counteract it (with a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+19 #Counteract]]{+19}).
tWwpnS8heqbG9VQe.name: Sacrilegious Aura

Toxic Exhaust Vents.description: In an effort to dispose of the PCs, the szynegation hub reroutes its exhaust systems to pump toxic fumes into this room.
Toxic Exhaust Vents.hazardDisable: @Check[athletics|dc:24] to plug the vents with nearby debris, @Check[crafting|dc:22] (trained) or @Check[thievery|dc:22] (trained) on the vent to deactivate the trap, or @Check[computers|dc:24] (trained) to Hack and reverse the flow of exhaust. There are two vents in this room. Once both have been disabled, the toxic fumes clear after 3 rounds. While these fumes persist, PCs need to hold their breath or rely on environmental protections in their armor; otherwise, they risk suffocating on the toxic fumes.
Toxic Exhaust Vents.hazardReset: The trap deactivates and resets after 1 minute.
Toxic Exhaust Vents.hazardRoutine: (1 action) The trap launches exhaust plume strikes against every creature in the room as 1 action. Because it launches exhaust continuously, the trap can also use the Oppressive Exhaust free action (see below) against each creature during that creature's turn.
Toxic Exhaust Vents.name: Toxic Exhaust Vents

Trenladoralis.description: Though rarely encountered outside their crumbling, relic-filled lairs, Akashic dragons occasionally live in hubs of knowledge, such as bustling space stations or cities. These dragons, bestowed with a direct connection to the Akashic Record, are arrogant curators of knowledge, assuming (often correctly) that no other being could possibly have a deeper understanding of the universe's secrets. Akashic dragons spend extensive time in the Akashic Record, often emerging after what they perceive as many days while mere hours have passed for the rest of the galaxy.

1glFKWbEEHLBydZu.description:
90 feet. The swirl of constant uploads and downloads near the Akashic dragon make attempts to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} unpredictable. A creature other than an akashic dragon that enters or begins its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to this dragon's Akashic interference for 1 minute.

Critical Success For 1 round, when the creature attempts to Recall Knowledge, it gains a +3 status bonus to its check.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure For 1 round, when the creature attempts to Recall Knowledge, it takes a –3 status penalty to its check.

Critical Failure As failure, but the effect lasts 1 minute.
1glFKWbEEHLBydZu.name: Akashic Interference

3T8rhNzByQZrJDhv.description:
Requirements The dragon has successfully Recalled Knowledge about an enemy within 90 feet within the last minute

Effect The dragon utters a shocking truth about the creature that even it might not know, causing it and its allies to hesitate or act erratically. Every enemy within 90 feet that can hear the secret must attempt a @Check[will|dc:31|options:area-effect,inflicts:slowed] save. Each creature is then immune to Shocking Revelation for 24 hours.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round.
3T8rhNzByQZrJDhv.name: Shocking Revelation

6bTILS2YSW9jQYQP.description: The first time each encounter the Akashic dragon hits and deals damage to a creature with their jaws Strike, they receive information about the creature as if they'd succeeded at a check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about that creature.
6bTILS2YSW9jQYQP.name: Records of the Enemy

Ie2A6VEeEAaPtoW6.description: Instead of using their own memories, an Akashic dragon can ascertain information from the Akashic Records. This gives it the Akashic Record Lore skill, which it can use to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} of any kind.
Ie2A6VEeEAaPtoW6.name: Akashic Eye

TeLCvv4q7TIPOXQD.description:
Trenladoralis takes on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change her Speed or attack and damage bonuses with her Strikes but might change the damage type her Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]
TeLCvv4q7TIPOXQD.name: Change Shape

YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.description: The Akashic dragon can activate magic and tech items with the Cast a Spell activation of any tradition as if the spells they contain were occult spells.
YNphbFGydAAzaQWx.name: Akashic Adaptability

fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.description:
You execute a psychic search of the Akashic Record for information about a specific topic and magically transfer this data to your comm unit or computer. When you Cast this Spell, choose any skill in which you're trained that has the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} action.

Any time during the duration, you can consult your comm unit while attempting a Recall Knowledge check using your chosen skill. This check gains a +1 status bonus. Checking your comm unit is part of the action to Recall Knowledge. You must be holding the comm unit to do so. The comm unit instantly compiles and displays snippets and selections from various media relevant to the topic, which grants you the bonus. If you roll a critical failure on this check, you get a failure instead. If the check is successful and the subject is a creature, you gain additional information or context about the creature. Once you reference the comm unit, the spell ends. When the spell ends, your access to the Akashic Record ends, and all the information you downloaded returns to the Akashic Record.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.h1i8c47U0IOrMrHJ]{Spell Effect: Akashic Download}

Heightened (3rd) You can reference your comm unit three times before the spell ends.
fPRg27BqEAJ6Md6V.name: Akashic Download (at will)

jgthYrZ2jNZoV5Ta.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

mdIGB9kjmEzFiA0k.description:
Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.
mdIGB9kjmEzFiA0k.name: Interplanar Teleport (at will; self only; to and from Akashic Record and the Universe only)

qYYH8A3ZYE1GohYf.description: The dragon condenses cutting truths and fiery revelations from the Akashic Record into sizzling laser fire that they project as a cone from their primary eye to assail their foes. This deals @Damage[14d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] (@Check[reflex|dc:33|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save). If a creature critically fails its Reflex save against Akashic Barrage and the Akashic dragon has succeeded at a check to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about the creature in the last minute, the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round. The dragon can't use Akashic Barrage again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Akashic Barrage]]{1d4 rounds}.
qYYH8A3ZYE1GohYf.name: Akashic Barrage

wZKJvFmBzPesW2Dv.description:
Trigger The dragon is critically hit by an attack

Effect The Akashic dragon raises a web of deflecting lasers using the eyes embedded all over their body, gaining resistance 15 to all damage against the triggering attack and absorbing some of the blow's energy, recharging their Akashic Barrage. If the Akashic dragon has succeeded at a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} check against the creature in the last minute, they gain resistance 20 instead.
wZKJvFmBzPesW2Dv.name: Deflecting Lasers

Trenladoralis.name: Trenladoralis
Trenladoralis.npcAllSaves: +2 status to all saves vs. occult

Unstable Teleporter.description: The runes embossed on the magitech teleportation circle glow and spark with uncontrolled magical energy. Bits of rubble and other unattended objects teleport randomly around the room.
Unstable Teleporter.hazardDisable: @Check[arcana|dc:25] to restabilize the teleportation pad, @Check[crafting|dc:25] or @Check[thievery|dc:25] to disable the hazard by hand, or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (4th rank; counteract DC 22) to counteract the effect; the ambient magic burns out and the hazard automatically disables after 1 minute
Unstable Teleporter.hazardRoutine: (1 action) Each creature within 50 feet of the teleporter must attempt a @Check[will|dc:25] save; on a failure, the target is teleported 10 feet in a random direction (but not through walls). This effect has the teleportation trait.
Unstable Teleporter.name: Unstable Teleporter

Vedzax.description:
Vedzaxes are the fast attack units of the Krethiskar subcolony. These small, winged components have four legs, each ending in a viciously jagged talon with which they can stab prey and pin them in place. A flock of vedzax often forms the vanguard of a Swarm attack force, swooping in from above to harry and distract targets while slower, more powerful Swarm units move into position.

The Krethiskar Swarm has developed new types of Swarm components to further its goals in the Szandite Collective systems.

934swptddSpn5mI8.description: A vedzax can sense nearby creatures through vibrations in air or water caused by movement as an imprecise sense at the listed range.
934swptddSpn5mI8.name: Motion Sense

N8vE7CE6Akr8zbMX.description:
Trigger An enemy successfully hits the vedzax with a melee Strike

Effect The vedzax Flies up to half its fly Speed.
N8vE7CE6Akr8zbMX.name: Soaring Retreat

k8S7PAgFioSLEtCg.description: The vedzax Flies up to its speed in a straight line, descending by at least 10 feet, then makes two talon Strikes. The vedzax deals an additional 1d6 acid damage with each of these Strikes.
k8S7PAgFioSLEtCg.name: Thrashing Dive

vjnwJQRkI3rHhnvZ.description: 30 feet. All allies with colony mind within the listed range of each other are in constant telepathic communication and are aware of all threats any individual knows about. While within range of at least one ally with colony mind, when a creature rolls a success on a save against a mental effect, it gets a critical success instead.
vjnwJQRkI3rHhnvZ.name: Colony Mind

Vedzax.name: Vedzax
